Native/text/legacy Chat schema projection narrows by operation and environment; ordinary Chat LSP is withheld both at schema and dispatch because hostFallbackAllowed is isolation, not action authority. Direct embedded lspTool/localTools admission remains opaque; its LspClient spawn is sanitized with getSafeEnv.

Ordinary Chat uses compiled AGENTS/optional ENGINEERING context; Plan/Deep catalog resolver/compiler paths are separate. LiveSession manifests track Chat delivered fragments; catalog/docs registration is not per-request evidence.

Failed/indeterminate mutation effects prevent no-change; process and await calls require explicit confirmed_no_change; cached verifier reuse records confirmed_no_change; child exceptions record indeterminate.

resolvedChecks: Native completion rejection feedback appears on the next native request, changes the model action, and cold reconstruction preserves controller provenance/non-authority: chatHarnessFeedback.test.ts test “rejected native completion feedback is controller-owned, durable, and changes the next provider action” (3 provider calls).

Twelve nonoverlapping ranges on one file keep read_range available and finish NO_CHANGE_REQUIRED without mutation: chatHarnessFeedback.test.ts test “fresh nonoverlapping ranges on one file preserve inspection and reach natural completion”.
Repetition loop detection emits only a progress_policy diagnostic; ordinary phase-nudge injection is removed; stall intervention is gated on absence of receipt deltas.

Retirement race: paused old governed write cannot restore live verifier certification after retire; same-task handoff remains live before retirement: toolExecutor.h4live.test.ts task-scoped live certification tests.

No-change gate rejects run_command/test_run/await_command with missing effect_status and accepts only explicit confirmed_no_change alongside successful inspection: chatOperationExplicit.test.ts “no-change completion requires real inspection and never certifies a patch”.

Cached verifier reuse logs effect_status confirmed_no_change only after cache identity/write-count/workspace-binding checks: chatEngineActionExecutor.ts cached receipt branch; broader cache tests in chatEngine.test.ts.

Both restricted native modes omit finish while text compatibility still recognizes it: chatToolDefinitions.test.ts “keeps legacy finish compatibility out of restricted native schemas” and chatEngineStall.test.ts restricted-set assertions.
Ordinary Chat LSP is unavailable at schema and action dispatch because canUseChatLsp always denies until lease-governed adapter exists; separate localTools lspTool route remains opaque.

LSP discovery no longer executes npx or candidates; installed server candidates resolve without process execution, and eventual LspClient spawn retains getSafeEnv: services/lsp/manager.test.ts and client.ts:start.

Green explicit verifier after inspected no-change uses repository scope only with content-bound Git state; dirty and untracked-byte edits mark it stale, missing Git state returns no receipt, and nonempty mutation paths stay file-scoped: chatEngineActionExecutor.ts:1687-1690, chatEngineVerifierAdapter.noChange.test.ts, chatRevisionBinding.ts currency/adaptation.

resolvedChecks.question: Does repository-scope revision capture correctly bind a nested Git project, exclude outside content, and fail closed on symlink-parent escapes while accepting known deleted parents?
resolvedChecks.resolution: Yes. readGitTree resolves physical Git top-level and project root, uses a :(top,literal) project pathspec, validates returned paths and each physical parent, and marks missing deleted-parent paths as known missing. Nested A→B dirty and untracked bytes affect the project revision; outside-root changes do not.

resolvedChecks.question: Can historical receipt metadata with unknown/missing scope or Git-binding currency remain green?
resolvedChecks.resolution: No. Receipt refresh marks an unevaluable revision stale; required repository binding also fails stale when Git identity/tree is unavailable. Explicit non-Git file-scoped receipts remain adaptable.
